segments.expected: "That's not three," said Anwen. "No. It's one. And whatever Talley cuts." Kiva held her wet right hand against her coat. "And in the third, if it's close, we try the hurdle again. With our wrists and our elbows, and no fingers at all." Pru was looking at her own hands, at the crooks of her elbows. She lifted her forearms together in front of her, as a girl lifts them to carry a basket of washing on her arms, and looked at the gap between them.

segments.expected: "I'm saying it again." Pru looked at her own arms, and then at Kiva. "I didn't call that. You didn't call that either. We just both did it." She held up her bleeding fingertips. "That's the first thing I've ever done in a lane that wasn't on somebody's word." Kiva looked at her. She thought of the yard behind the Long Quay on Sunday, and Pike saying from a tailboard, you call from the air before you've landed, and Pru on a seeding floor calling hands off, left before the Tarn's carry had moved. "It wasn't on anybody's," she said. "That's why it worked."

segments.expected: The board went up at six with Thursday's twelve lanes on it. Kiva read it at the back of the crowd with Pru beside her and Perrin behind, under the lamp, while the tide went out of the timber pond's black water under the boards. Every one of the twelve lanes had gone to the four that stood higher. The Tarn's first four had stood with Trewin on frosted feet and a reserve at Bridie's place, and had won by a single point and the glass. Halden License had beaten the twenty-fourth six to two. The Ropewalk's seven to nothing stood at the head of the column, alone. Team Seven (9) beat the Tarn, second four (16). Seven to two.
